$comment: D-CSUBSET-WEAK-EXTERN-IMPORT-NOT-IN-SYMBOL-TABLE (P54): the RUN witness for a WEAK extern IMPORT nothing in the program defines. `&ea` must resolve to NULL (the else arm, +7) while an ordinary global's address must not (+35) -- 7 + 35 = 42, so reversing EITHER branch changes the exit code and the two cannot mask each other. Before this row closed, `weak` on an extern import reached the HIR linkage map and STOPPED (HIR->MIR consumed the map for function definitions and globals only), so every emitted object marked the undefined symbol STRONG and every DSS-linked image REFUSED the program with K_SymbolUndefined -- a loud refusal of a program gcc, clang and (on PE) clang-through-mingw-ld all link and run. ✔MEASURED at this tree, all four arms: elf64-x86_64 rc 42, elf64-aarch64 under qemu rc 42, pe64-x86_64 rc 42; the darwin arm is built on every host and RUN on the macOS leg. ★ THE `release` ARM IS NOT DECORATION HERE: the null resolution has to survive the optimizer, and a pass that assumed the address of a declared object is never null would fold `if (&ea)` to TRUE, take the read arm and load through the null slot -- a crash or a wrong exit, never 42. RED-on-disable: delete `__attribute__((weak))` from `ea`'s declaration -> the reference is STRONG, nothing defines it, and the link refuses with K_SymbolUndefined on every leg (no artifact at all, so no exit code). ⓘ HOW THE NULL IS SPELLED, because it is NOT 'give the symbol address 0': every reference to an extern DATA import is lowered got-indirect (the code materializes a POINTER SLOT and dereferences it), so the link gives the symbol a pointer-sized read-only slot whose CONTENT is 0. ✔MEASURED the alternative first -- binding the symbol itself at address 0 produced an ELF exec that linked clean and SEGFAULTED (rc 139), because the deref hit address 0. clang spells it the same way on PE (`.refptr.ea` in `.rdata`), and ld leaves an unresolved weak symbol's GOT slot zero on ELF.
